perf.summary: BFS queue q is stackalloc'd inside while(true); level[] is allocated and initialized but never used.
perf.currentCost: stackalloc int[n] q per outer iteration; plus `int* level = stackalloc int[n]; for(i) level[i]=0;` — level is written once and never read anywhere in the method (dead allocation + dead O(n) init loop).
perf.proposedChange: Remove the level array and its init loop entirely. Hoist q stackalloc above the while(true) loop and reset qh/qt per iteration.
perf.rationale: Eliminates a full O(n) stackalloc plus its zeroing loop that produce nothing, and reduces outer-loop allocations to one. Pure dead-code removal is a guaranteed win.
perf.risk: None — level is provably unused (write-only); removing it cannot change outputs.

perf.summary: Repeated reduced-cost subexpression pot[u]-pot[v] and cost[e] recompute; hoist pot[u] out of the edge loop.
perf.currentCost: Inside the per-node edge scan, `dist[u] + cost[e] + pot[u] - pot[v]` recomputes dist[u]+pot[u] for every outgoing edge of u.
perf.proposedChange: Hoist `long base = dist[u] + pot[u];` once per node before the edge loop, then `long nd = base + cost[e] - pot[v];`. Same hoist applies in Spfa and Dijkstra inner loops.
perf.rationale: Removes one add and one load (dist[u], pot[u]) per edge from the inner loop, shortening the dependency chain of the relaxation test.
perf.risk: None — dist[u] and pot[u] are invariant across u's edge scan (not mutated inside the loop body for the current u).
